blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A notification service sends each message through three methods with instanceof chains over Email and Sms, in this order: maxLength() ends with `return 10_000;`, costCents() ends with `throw new IllegalArgumentException();`, and render() ends with `return text;`. A developer adds a Push channel and a Push branch in render() only, then sends a 300-character push; push allows 240. What happens?

options.text: The push fails in costCents() with an exception, since that chain's last line throws for a type it doesn't name
options.says: a chain's fallback answers a missed type silently (maxLength() returns 10_000); a chain ending in a throw fails when the path runs

options.text: The push goes out at 300 characters and costs nothing, since maxLength() and costCents() answer it from their last lines
options.says: costCents() ends with a throw, so the push fails there at run time; only maxLength() answers from a fallback

options.text: The build stops at maxLength(), since javac reports a chain whose last line answers a type it doesn't name
options.says: javac checks nothing about an instanceof chain; the page's missed copies compiled

options.text: The build stops at costCents(), since javac reports a chain whose last line throws for a type it doesn't name
options.says: javac checks nothing about an instanceof chain; the throw happens at run time, as the page's refund() did

origin.section: A Type Check Copied Into Several Methods Still Compiles When One Copy Is Missed

questions.stem: invoicing.jar contains Invoicer, compiled against an interface TaxRule { long taxCents(long netCents); }. A year later a team ships ReverseCharge implements TaxRule in its own jar and passes an instance to Invoicer, with invoicing.jar unchanged on the classpath. What happens?

options.text: It fails until Invoicer is rebuilt, since Invoicer's class file was compiled before ReverseCharge existed
options.says: the page runs a caller's unchanged class file against a type compiled after it

options.text: It fails with NoClassDefFoundError, since ReverseCharge was not on Invoicer's compile classpath
options.says: Invoicer never names ReverseCharge; it calls the interface, and the class is found on the run-time classpath

options.text: It works with Invoicer as shipped, since Invoicer's call names TaxRule and the object supplies the body
options.says: the page compiles Wallet after Checkout and runs it through the unchanged Checkout.class, same hash before and after

options.text: It works with Invoicer as shipped, since the JVM finds ReverseCharge through its jar's service listing
options.says: no service listing is involved; Invoicer is handed the object, and the interface call is dispatched on it, as the page's unchanged Checkout.class shows

origin.section: Put the Behaviour on the Type, and a New Type Is One New Class That javac Checks

questions.stem: A reporting library's public interface ExportFormat has 5 implementations in the library and 2 in customers' plug-in jars. The library adds `String mediaType();` to ExportFormat, implements it in its own 5 classes, and releases. A customer upgrades the library without rebuilding the plug-ins and runs an export through one of them. What happens?

options.text: It throws when the library calls mediaType(), since the plug-in's class has no body for that method
options.says: the page runs GiftCard, built against the old interface, and the new method throws AbstractMethodError when called

options.text: It throws when the library calls mediaType(), since the JVM returns null for the missing body and the export uses it
options.says: there is no null result: the call itself throws AbstractMethodError, as GiftCard's did

options.text: It throws when the plug-in class is loaded, since the JVM checks each class against its interfaces' methods
options.says: the page's GiftCard object was created and printed; the error came at the call to the new method

options.text: It throws when the plug-in class is loaded, since its class file names an interface version that no longer exists
options.says: class files name the interface, not a version of it; GiftCard loaded against the new interface

origin.section: An Interface Is Closed to a New Operation: Adding One Edits Every Implementation

questions.stem: A sealed interface Shipment permits Parcel and Pallet. Three methods switch over it: price() and label() have a case for each type, and customsForm() has `case Parcel p -> "CN22"; default -> "none";`. The team adds Container to the permits list and a case to price() only, then builds. Which methods does javac report?

options.text: label() and customsForm(), since a default branch doesn't count for a type added after it was written
options.says: a default covers every type, including later ones, so customsForm() compiles and answers "none" for a container

options.text: label() only, since the default branch in customsForm() already covers every permitted type
options.says: the page's run reports each switch without a default; a default makes a switch exhaustive whatever the permits list says

options.text: customsForm() only, since a default over a sealed type hides a case the compiler has to flag
options.says: a default is allowed over a sealed type and switches the check off; label() is the switch javac reports

options.text: Neither of them, since a new permitted type is checked only at run time, with MatchException
options.says: recompiled code gets the compile error the page shows; run-time behaviour against the old permits list is unit 1.5.4's

origin.section: When the Types Are Fixed and the Operations Grow, Seal the Hierarchy and Let javac List the Switches

questions.stem: A team plugs a processor into the module's ConcurrentPipeline. Its process(sku) looks the price up in a HashMap field and fills the map on a miss. The pipeline uses a ReentrantLock in processItem() and runs each item on a virtual thread through processAll(). Is the processor's map safe?

options.text: Yes, since processItem() holds the pipeline's lock while it calls process()
options.says: the page shows the pipeline calling process() outside its lock, which guards only its result list

options.text: Yes, since processAll() holds the pipeline's lock around the whole batch
options.says: process() runs from many threads at once outside the lock, so no lock is held around the batch

options.text: No, since each item's virtual thread works on its own fresh copy of the map
options.says: all threads call the same processor object, so they share one map; that sharing is the problem

options.text: No, since process() runs on several threads at once while no lock is held
options.says: the page shows a plain counter in process() losing updates under processAll(), while a LongAdder counts exactly

origin.section: A Closed Pipeline Still Runs Every Extension on Its Own Threads

concepts: A closed pipeline calls a plugged-in processor from many threads outside its own lock, so the processor's own state needs its own thread safety.

Adding an operation to an interface edits every implementation; an implementation compiled against the old interface throws AbstractMethodError when the new method is called, and a default method gives every type the same answer.
A default branch in a switch over a sealed type makes it compile when a permitted type is added, so javac no longer reports it.
